title: Twice as hot, not twice as fast
hook: Double the kelvins of the air. Do its molecules move twice as fast?

knows: that air is made of moving molecules
that the kelvin scale starts at absolute zero and K = °C + 273
doesNotKnow: that temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the molecules
that molecular speed grows as the square root of the absolute temperature

misconception: Doubling the temperature doubles the speed of the molecules (and 20 °C to 40 °C is 'twice as hot').
objective: The learner can explain that temperature tracks energy of motion, which grows with speed squared, so doubling the kelvin temperature multiplies the typical speed by √2 ≈ 1.41, and four times the kelvins doubles it.

claims.text: For an ideal gas the average kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2) k T, so the root-mean-square speed is √(3kT/m) and grows as the square root of the kelvin temperature.
claims.source: Kinetic theory of gases: Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry (kinetic model of gases, v_rms = (3RT/M)^1/2).

claims.text: The typical (root-mean-square) speed of air molecules is about 510 m/s at 300 K and about 720 m/s at 600 K.
claims.source: v_rms = sqrt(3 k T / m), k = 1.380649e-23 J/K (SI 2019, exact), m = 28.97e-3 kg/mol / 6.02214076e23 (mean molar mass of dry air 28.96-28.97 g/mol, U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976). 300 K: 508 m/s; 600 K: 719 m/s; 1,200 K: 1,016 m/s (node script). The stage rounds to 10 m/s.

claims.text: Going from 300 K to 600 K multiplies the typical speed by √2 ≈ 1.41; reaching twice the speed takes four times the kelvins, 1,200 K.
300 K is about 27 °C, 600 K about 327 °C, 1,200 K about 927 °C; 27 °C to 54 °C is 300 K to 327 K.
claims.source: T(°C) = T(K) - 273.15 (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed., 2019); the stage rounds with 273.

claims.text: The box is a flat (2-D) model with 30 molecules and a seeded spread of speeds; their on-screen speeds scale exactly as √T, but the picture is illustrative, not a measurement.
claims.source: Representation choice: every molecule's screen speed is multiplied by sqrt(T / 300 K).

recall.question: A gas goes from 200 K to 800 K. Its molecules' typical speed becomes about…
recall.why: Speed grows as the square root of the kelvin temperature: √(800/200) = √4 = 2.
